result.strongest_objection: The proposed no-follow guarantee covers only a symlink at the final path component. If Git tracks d/f and the quiescent worktree replaces d with a symlink to an external directory, enumeration still yields d/f; leaf type checks and batched shasum can follow d and read external content. This violates the stated filesystem boundary without any concurrent writer.
result.catch: V6/V9 test leaf symlinks, not symlinked ancestors of tracked paths. They do not establish the unconditional claims that symlinks are never dereferenced and snapshots never read outside the worktree.
result.proposed_fix: Add this rule: 'Under the quiescent-tree assumption, validate every ancestor component of each eligible root-relative path beneath the physical worktree root before inspecting or hashing its leaf. Reject symlinked or non-directory ancestors with snapshot_error; genuinely missing ancestors represent an absent path. Only final-component symlinks may be hashed as link text.' Add a hermetic regression that commits d/f, replaces d with a symlink to an external directory containing f, and verifies rc 15 before external content is opened. Include an external blocking-target variant and an auditable verification-log row. Narrow the no-follow guarantee explicitly to the documented quiescent-tree assumption.

result.strongest_objection: The `worktree_changed_files` distinct path count algorithm is mathematically flawed as specified. Running `comm -23` and `comm -13` on the manifest files compares entire lines (path + tag). Since an edited file's tag changes, its entire line changes, causing `comm` to falsely count it as both deleted (old line unique to before) and created (new line unique to after). Summing this with the `join` output will incorrectly count a single edited file 3 times, contradicting the spec's claim that it reports 1.
result.catch: The `comm` commands must strictly operate on path-only projections, whereas `join` must operate on the full manifests to compare tags.
result.proposed_fix: Revise the distinct-path count definition to explicitly project paths: "Extract path lists (`cut -f1 manifest > paths`). `comm -23 before.paths after.paths` (deleted) + `comm -13 before.paths after.paths` (created) + `join -t '\t' -1 1 before.manifest after.manifest | awk -F'\t' '$2 != $3'` (edited)."

result.strongest_objection: The consumer-surface claim ('rc 15 needs no consumer code change') is under-verified. V13's grep only searched `.claude/skills/mission-control/`, but the doc itself references `nightly_classify.py`, `eval_harness/metrics.go`, and `.claude/skills/mission-control/resources/codex-lane-false-greens.md` — files that exist outside or at the edge of that scope. The doc asserts these are 'unrelated to the pi verdict' without a verification command proving they do not contain an explicit exit-code switch (case/if/elif) over `0/10/11/12/13/14` that would misclassify or crash on `15`. If any such consumer has a fall-through default that is not 'treat as LANE FAILURE' (e.g., log-and-continue, retry-on-unknown, or a hard `case` with no `*` arm), rc 15 silently changes behavior. The grep scope is insufficient to support a 'no consumer code change' conclusion.

It does not cover the full repo, does not grep the actual files it names (`nightly_classify.py`, `metrics.go`), and does not verify that `codex-lane-false-greens.md` (listed under Related Documents as documenting verdict behavior) lacks an explicit code enumeration that needs updating alongside the two 'source-of-truth' comments already identified.
result.proposed_fix: Add a verification-log row (V14) that runs a repo-wide grep: `grep -rn 'mission_pi_run\|empty_worktree\|worktree_changed_files\|snapshot_error' --include='*.py' --include='*.go' --include='*.sh' --include='*.md' .` and report every hit. For each hit outside the already-handled `SKILL.md:1403-1445`, add a row stating whether it contains an explicit exit-code switch over pi verdict codes and how rc 15 falls through. If `nightly_classify.py` or `metrics.go` parse the pi verdict JSON or exit code, either verify their default arm is 'treat as failure' or add them to the code-changes list. If `codex-lane-false-greens.md` enumerates the verdict codes, add it to the doc-comment update list alongside the two source-of-truth comments.
